name: Blackwell Horizons Dispersed Primitive Camping Area - Hoosier National Forest

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Hoosier National Forest Headquarters

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted at Blackwell Horizons clearing near the Charles C. Deam Wilderness border. Campsites set back 100ft from trails and ponds.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6-8 inches deep in rich organic soil, at least 200 feet from ponds or trails. Pack out all paper products.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace. Pack out all waste.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in established rock fire rings only. Extinguish cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey Indiana DNR / USFS fire alerts.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved state road changing to well-graded gravel forest road (Tower Ridge Road / FS 15)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Smooth gravel main ridge road; easy access.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (easily accessible year-round)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 55-70°F, blooming dogwood and redbud, occasional rainstorms.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot and humid (80-88°F), lush green forest, high insect activity.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Stunning Midwest autumn colors (55-70°F daytime, 40-50°F nights), ideal camping.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cool 30-45°F, freezing nights, occasional snow dustings.

dangers_and_hazards: Ticks and chiggers in high grass during warm months
Falling tree limbs during high winds

common_human_made_sounds: Occasional horse trailer driving to Deam Wilderness trailhead

common_plants_and_trees: Yellow Poplar / Tulip Tree (Indiana State Tree)

human_demographics_and_culture: Backcountry backpackers (Deam Wilderness), equestrian riders, digital nomads from Bloomington, and stargazers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Miami and Shawnee indigenous traditions revere the ancient hardwood hills of southern Indiana as sacred hunting and peaceful gathering grounds.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Open ridge solar vitality, peaceful hardwood forest atmosphere.

nearby_hiking_trails.trail_name: Grubb Ridge Loop Trail (Charles C. Deam Wilderness)
nearby_hiking_trails.features: Winding wilderness trail through oak-hickory forest and stream valleys

public_reviews_summary: Extremely accessible free primitive camping spot in Indiana. Outstanding 5G cell coverage and easy driving distance to Bloomington.
other_data: Bortle Class 3 night sky. Great solar panel placement in open meadow.
